front.text: Who became king in 1066 after the Battle of Hastings?
front.markdown: Who became **king** in **1066** after the **Battle of Hastings**?

back.text: William I, later known as William the Conqueror, ruled 1066–1087.
back.markdown:
## William I the Conqueror

{#0F766E}He was Duke of Normandy and defeated Harold II at Hastings.{/}

- Reign: **1066–1087**
- Famous for: **Norman Conquest** of England and commissioning the **Domesday Book**

front.text: Who ruled England from 1087 to 1100 and was nicknamed 'Rufus'?
front.markdown: Who ruled from **1087–1100** and was nicknamed **“Rufus”**?

back.markdown:
## William II (Rufus)

{#0F766E}Known as **William II** and called **William Rufus** for his red hair or complexion.{/}

- Reign: **1087–1100**
- Died unexpectedly while hunting in the New Forest

front.text: Which king reigned from 1100 to 1135 and was called 'Lion of Justice'?
front.markdown: Which king reigned **1100–1135** and was called **“Lion of Justice”**?

back.text: Henry I, third child of William I, ruled from 1100–1135.
back.markdown:
## Henry I

{#0F766E}Henry I is often remembered for strengthening royal justice and government.{/}

- Reign: **1100–1135**
- Nickname: **“Lion of Justice”**
- Died without surviving male heir, leading to a succession crisis

front.text: Who ruled during the period known as 'The Anarchy'?
front.markdown: Who ruled during the conflict called **“The Anarchy”**?

back.text: King Stephen (1135–1154), a nephew of Henry I.
back.markdown:
## Stephen of Blois

{#C62828}His reign was marked by civil war between supporters of Stephen and Empress Matilda.{/}

- Reign: **1135–1154**
- Conflict called: **The Anarchy**
- Ended with **Treaty of Wallingford** allowing Matilda's son to inherit

front.text: Who began the long Plantagenet dynasty in 1154?
front.markdown: Who began the long **Plantagenet** dynasty in **1154**?

back.markdown:
## Henry II

{#0F766E}Founder of the Plantagenet line and the first king after Stephen's reign ended in compromise.{/}

- Reign: **1154–1189**
- Set early groundwork for common law and royal administration

front.text: Which king was known for crusades and ruled 1189–1199?
front.markdown: Which king ruled **1189–1199** and was famous for leading the **Third Crusade**?

back.text: Richard I, called the Lionheart, ruled 1189–1199.
back.markdown:
## Richard I (Lionheart)

{#0F766E}Popularly known as **Richard the Lionheart** for his battlefield reputation.{/}

- Reign: **1189–1199**
- Spent much of his reign campaigning in the **Crusades**
- Spent little time ruling in England itself

front.text: Who signed Magna Carta and ruled from 1199 to 1216?
front.markdown: Who signed **Magna Carta** and ruled from **1199–1216**?

back.markdown:
## King John

{#C62828}His conflicts with nobles led directly to the 1215 signing of Magna Carta at Runnymede.{/}

- Reign: **1199–1216**
- Magna Carta: **1215**
- Also called **John Lackland** after losing French territories

front.text: Who ruled from 1216 to 1272 and was a child during his accession?
front.markdown: Which king ruled **1216–1272** after ascending young?

back.markdown:
## Henry III

{#0F766E}Henry III was crowned as a child after the death of King John.{/}

- Reign: **1216–1272**
- Longest reigning king of his era
- Era marked by conflicts with barons and baronial reform

front.text: Which king (1272–1307) expanded royal authority and built famous castles?
front.markdown: Who ruled **1272–1307** and strengthened royal power?

back.text: Edward I, known for wars in Wales and Scotland.
back.markdown:
## Edward I

{#0F766E}Often called **Edward Longshanks** for his height and rule through law and war.{/}

- Reign: **1272–1307**
- Built strong royal institutions and castles including in Wales
- Key conflict with Scotland under William Wallace and Robert the Bruce

front.text: Which king (1307–1327) faced deposition and was seen as weak in court politics?
front.markdown: Which king ruled **1307–1327** and was deposed after conflict with nobles?

back.markdown:
## Edward II

{#C62828}His reign is remembered for battlefield losses and deep noble resentment.{/}

- Reign: **1307–1327**
- Deposed by a coalition led by queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer
- Follows a turbulent and unstable period

front.text: Who ruled the longest among early Edwardians, from 1327–1377?
front.markdown: Who ruled from **1327–1377**, the longest of the early Edwards?

back.markdown:
## Edward III

{#0F766E}Reign began in youth and lasted a full **50 years**—long for medieval England.{/}

- Reign: **1327–1377**
- Led England during the start of the **Hundred Years’ War**
- Known for military and courtly developments

front.text: Which king reigned 1377–1399 and was deposed by Henry IV?
front.markdown: Who reigned **1377–1399** and was deposed by **Henry Bolingbroke**?

back.text: Richard II was deposed in 1399 and replaced by Henry IV.
back.markdown:
## Richard II

{#C62828}Richard II’s rule ended in 1399 when Henry IV seized the crown after conflict and exile.{/}

- Reign: **1377–1399**
- One of the last medieval kings to be deposed rather than merely replaced by succession
- Central figure in the transition from Plantagenet to Lancastrian rule

front.text: Who was the first Lancastrian king, ruling from 1399 to 1413?
front.markdown: Who was the first **Lancastrian** king (1399–1413)?

back.text: Henry IV, beginning the Lancastrian line.
back.markdown:
## Henry IV

{#0F766E}His reign began by taking the crown from Richard II.{/}

- Reign: **1399–1413**
- Founder of the **House of Lancaster** phase within the Plantagenet period
- First king to rule from the claim of Bolingbroke bloodline

front.text: Which king ruled 1413–1422 and won Agincourt?
front.markdown: Which king ruled **1413–1422** and won at **Agincourt**?

back.markdown:
## Henry V

{#0F766E}Henry V is celebrated for the **Battle of Agincourt** in 1415 during the Hundred Years’ War.{/}

- Reign: **1413–1422**
- Famous victory: **Agincourt (1415)**
- Strong symbol of military kingship in English memory

front.text: Who ruled during two separate periods during the Wars of the Roses (1422–1471)?
front.markdown: Which king ruled from **1422–1471**, with a break in between?

back.markdown:
## Henry VI

{#C62828}Henry VI’s reign was interrupted by civil conflict between York and Lancaster factions.{/}

- Reign periods: **1422–1461** and **1470–1471**
- Era characterized by mental illness episodes and weak central control
- The Wars of the Roses intensified under his weak kingship

front.text: Which king ruled in 1461 and was restored after a brief deposition?
front.markdown: Who ruled as king in **1461** from the House of York?

back.text: Edward IV, restored after brief interruption and central to Yorkist rule.
back.markdown:
## Edward IV

{#0F766E}A major Yorkist king who helped secure Lancastrian defeat at key moments.{/}

- Reign: **1461–1483**
- Exile and return helped shape **Wars of the Roses** outcomes
- Preceded the brief reign of Edward V and Richard III

front.text: Who was king for only a few months in 1483 before being deposed?
front.markdown: Who ruled for a short period in **1483** before being replaced?

back.text: Edward V, one of the youngest English monarchs to rule.
back.markdown:
## Edward V

{#C62828}Known for his brief reign and the mystery of his disappearance with his brother (the “Princes in the Tower”).{/}

- Reign: **April–July 1483**
- Never crowned
- Deposed in favor of his uncle Richard III

front.text: Which king reigned 1483–1485 and was the last Plantagenet king?
front.markdown: Which king reigned **1483–1485** and was the last **Plantagenet** king?

back.markdown:
## Richard III

{#0F766E}He was the last English king from the Plantagenet line.{/}

- Reign: **1483–1485**
- Died at the **Battle of Bosworth Field**
- Replaced by Henry VII, beginning the Tudor dynasty

front.text: Which king started the Tudor dynasty in 1485?
front.markdown: Who began the **Tudor dynasty** in **1485**?

back.markdown:
## Henry VII

{#0F766E}Founded the Tudor dynasty after defeating Richard III at Bosworth.{/}

- Reign: **1485–1509**
- Stabilized England after years of civil war
- Founder of the **Tudor royal line**

front.text: Who ruled 1509–1547 and oversaw the English Reformation?
front.markdown: Who ruled **1509–1547** and broke with Rome?

back.markdown:
## Henry VIII

{#C62828}His break with Rome created the Church of England and began major religious reordering.{/}

- Reign: **1509–1547**
- Broke from the **Catholic Church** in 1534
- Married six times and had three legitimate heirs

front.text: Which child king ruled from 1547–1553 as the first Tudor monarch to reign as Protestant?
front.markdown: Which monarch ruled **1547–1553** and was the first Tudor Protestant king?

back.markdown:
## Edward VI

{#0F766E}A child king whose short reign advanced Protestant reforms.{/}

- Reign: **1547–1553**
- Died at age 15
- Followed by the Catholic restoration under Mary I

front.text: Who ruled 1553–1558 and tried to restore Catholicism?
front.markdown: Who ruled **1553–1558** and is known for restoring Catholic practice?

back.markdown:
## Mary I

{#C62828}Called **“Bloody Mary”** by later Protestant opponents for religious persecution.{/}

- Reign: **1553–1558**
- Attempted to reverse the Protestant reforms of Edward VI
- Died without a surviving heir in 1558

front.text: Which queen reigned 1558–1603 and founded what many call the English Renaissance era at court?
front.markdown: Who reigned **1558–1603** and presided over a major cultural flowering?

back.markdown:
## Elizabeth I

{#0F766E}Reign is commonly associated with the **Elizabethan era**, diplomacy, and sea exploration.{/}

- Reign: **1558–1603**
- Known as the **Virgin Queen**
- Presided over the defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588

front.text: Who was the first Stuart king, beginning the move from England to a United Kingdom-style monarchy?
front.markdown: Who was the **first Stuart king** of England in **1603**?

back.markdown:
## James I

{#0F766E}He became king of England in 1603, uniting the crowns of England and Scotland under one ruler.{/}

- Reign: **1603–1625**
- Also known as **James VI of Scotland**
- Published ideas on monarchy in texts like the **Divine Right** tradition

front.text: Which king ruled from 1625 to 1649 and was executed after civil war?
front.markdown: Which king ruled **1625–1649** and was executed in 1649?

back.markdown:
## Charles I

{#C62828}Charles I’s conflict with Parliament led to the English Civil War and his execution.{/}

- Reign: **1625–1649**
- Tried-and-executed after defeat
- Led to temporary abolition of monarchy during the Interregnum

front.text: Who restored the monarchy in 1660?
front.markdown: Who restored the monarchy after the Interregnum in **1660**?

back.markdown:
## Charles II

{#0F766E}His period is remembered as the **Restoration**, when the monarchy returned after Oliver Cromwell’s republic.{/}

- Reign: **1660–1685**
- Also called **The Merry Monarch**
- Reinstated court culture and parliamentary monarchy after upheaval

front.text: Which king was deposed during the Glorious Revolution?
front.markdown: Which king was deposed in the **1688 Glorious Revolution**?

back.markdown:
## James II

{#C62828}James II was removed by Parliament and invited invaders in 1688, leading to constitutional change.{/}

- Reign: **1685–1688**
- Overthrown in favor of William and Mary
- Preceded stronger constitutional monarchy limits

front.text: Who ruled jointly with Mary II from 1689 to 1702?
front.markdown: Which king ruled jointly from **1689–1702**?

back.text: William III, co-ruling with Mary II (1689–1702).
back.markdown:
## William III (of Orange)

{#0F766E}His reign with Mary II is remembered for winning the war against France and the **Glorious Revolution** settlement.{/}

- Reign: **1689–1702**
- Co-ruler with **Mary II** from 1689–1694
- Strengthened constitutional balance between king and Parliament

front.text: Who was queen in 1689–1694 and ruled jointly with William III?
front.markdown: Who was the co-ruler queen with **William III**?

back.markdown:
## Mary II

{#0F766E}Mary II became co-sovereign with her husband William III, bringing legitimacy to the post-revolution settlement.{/}

- Reign: **1689–1694**
- Queen of England, Scotland, and Ireland
- Part of the **Glorious Revolution** transition

front.text: Which queen reigned 1702–1714 and was the last Stuart monarch?
front.markdown: Who reigned **1702–1714** and was the last of the Stuarts?

back.markdown:
## Queen Anne

{#0F766E}Anne was the last direct **Stuart** sovereign of Great Britain.{/}

- Reign: **1702–1714**
- Oversaw the **Acts of Union (1707)** creating the Kingdom of Great Britain
- Her death ended the main Stuart dynasty

front.text: Who was the first Hanoverian king in 1714?
front.markdown: Who became king in **1714** starting the Hanoverian line?

back.markdown:
## George I

{#0F766E}His accession followed Anne’s death under the 1701 Act of Settlement line of succession.{/}

- Reign: **1714–1727**
- First king of the **House of Hanover**
- First monarch with limited English fluency as a German-speaking ruler

front.text: Which king reigned 1727–1760 and presided over early empire expansion?
front.markdown: Which king ruled **1727–1760** during major imperial expansion?

back.markdown:
## George II

{#0F766E}George II’s reign included parliamentary power growth and expanding empire trade.{/}

- Reign: **1727–1760**
- First British monarch whose English government role was largely constitutional in practice
- Reign includes early growth of imperial global competition

front.text: Who ruled 1760–1820 across American independence and Napoleonic conflict?
front.markdown: Who reigned **1760–1820** through the American Revolution and Napoleonic era?

back.markdown:
## George III

{#C62828}Longest Hanoverian reign and the king during the American Revolution.{/}

- Reign: **1760–1820**
- Witnessed: **American Revolution (1775–1783)**
- Also ruled during the early Napoleonic period

front.text: Who became king in 1820 and was known for style and scandal in the Regency context?
front.markdown: Who became king in **1820** and was a major 19th-century court figure?

back.markdown:
## George IV

{#0F766E}George IV’s tastes shaped architecture, culture, and court spectacle in the early 1800s.{/}

- Reign: **1820–1830**
- Served as Prince Regent before kingship (1811–1820)
- Era linked to elegant neoclassical culture

front.text: Which king ruled 1830–1837 before Victoria and was called the 'Sailor King'?
front.markdown: Who ruled from **1830–1837** before Queen Victoria?

back.text: William IV, known as the Sailor King.
back.markdown:
## William IV

{#0F766E}William IV had a naval background and ruled for only seven years.{/}

- Reign: **1830–1837**
- Known as the **Sailor King**
- Succeeded by his niece Victoria

front.text: Who ruled 1837–1901 and had the longest reign until Elizabeth II?
front.markdown: Which monarch ruled **1837–1901** and later held the record for longest reign?

back.markdown:
## Queen Victoria

{#0F766E}She reigned during industrial expansion and colonial period; “Victorian era” still defines an age.{/}

- Reign: **1837–1901**
- Preceded the 20th-century constitutional monarchy form we know today
- Married Prince Albert (marriage in 1840)

front.text: Who became king in 1901 after Victoria and ruled until 1910?
front.markdown: Who became king in **1901** and reigned until **1910**?

back.text: Edward VII reigned from 1901–1910 and gave his name to the Edwardian era.
back.markdown:
## Edward VII

{#0F766E}He ushered in the Edwardian era, ending the long Victorian era.{/}

- Reign: **1901–1910**
- House: **Saxe-Coburg and Gotha**
- Era named for him: **Edwardian era**

front.text: Which king ruled 1910–1936 and was king through WWI?
front.markdown: Who ruled **1910–1936** and was king through World War I?

back.markdown:
## George V

{#0F766E}His reign included World War I and the 1917 renaming of the royal house.{/}

- Reign: **1910–1936**
- Changed family dynastic name from Saxe-Coburg-Gotha to **Windsor** in 1917
- Led monarchy through wartime transitions

front.text: Which king had the briefest reign of modern rulers, abdicating in 1936?
front.markdown: Who had the shortest modern reign and abdicated in **1936**?

back.text: Edward VIII, who abdicated the same year he became king.
back.markdown:
## Edward VIII

{#C62828}His abdication to marry Wallis Simpson made 1936 a year of constitutional shock.{/}

- Reign: **January–December 1936**
- Abdicated voluntarily (the **Abdication Crisis**)
- Succeeded by his brother George VI

front.text: Who became king after Edward VIII and reigned through WWII?
front.markdown: Who became king in 1936 after Edward VIII and ruled through World War II?

back.markdown:
## George VI

{#0F766E}His reign is tied to wartime morale and steady public leadership.{/}

- Reign: **1936–1952**
- Became king after his brother’s abdication
- Father of Elizabeth II

front.text: Which queen reigned from 1952 until 2022 and became Britain’s longest-reigning monarch?
front.markdown: Who reigned **1952–2022** and became Britain’s longest-reigning monarch?

back.text: Queen Elizabeth II, Britain’s longest-reigning monarch, reigned from 1952–2022.
back.markdown:
## Queen Elizabeth II

{#0F766E}Britain’s longest-reigning monarch, whose reign bridged postwar Britain and the modern media age.{/}

- Reign: **1952–2022**
- Reigned through decolonization, Cold War years, and major media modernization
- Succeeded by her son, **Charles III**

front.text: Who is the current king and what is the year of accession?
front.markdown: Who is the **current king** and when did he accede?

back.text: Charles III has been king since 8 September 2022.
back.markdown:
## King Charles III

{#0F766E}Current monarch as of August 2026, ascending after Queen Elizabeth II’s death.{/}

- Reign started: **8 September 2022**
- Coronation: **6 May 2023**
- Continues the constitutional monarch role with an elected government
